entries.name: #MANSION
entries.content:
Located on a gently rolling hill, the mansion is surrounded by extensive gardens and perfectly trimmed hedges. A long gravel driveway, flanked by centuries-old oak trees, leads to the main entrance. The façade is made of grey stone, with large sash windows and white wooden shutters. The architecture reflects the Georgian style, with its characteristic elegance and symmetry.
Upon entering, the foyer is spacious with black and white marble floors in a checkerboard pattern. An elegant spiral staircase with wrought iron railings and a dark wooden handrail leads to the upper floor. The high ceilings are adorned with antique mouldings and chandeliers that provide soft, warm lighting.
The main living room is decorated with emerald green velvet sofas and armchairs, mahogany coffee tables and a marble fireplace that takes up an entire wall. The walls are covered with tapestries and portraits of ancestors, while a grand piano sits in one corner, ready for late-night musical sessions.
The dining room is impressive, with a long oak table surrounded by leather-upholstered chairs. Staffordshire china and glassware sparkle under the light of a grand crystal chandelier. Formal dinners are common, with impeccable service and gourmet dishes prepared in a kitchen with classic period equipment such as Aga ovens and copper cookware.
The library is a haven of tranquility, with shelves filled with leather-bound books, a carved oak desk and comfortable armchairs for reading. An antique globe and silk-shaded table lamps add a touch of elegance.
The bedrooms are sanctuaries of luxury, with four-poster beds, fine linen bedding and Persian rugs. Windows offer panoramic views of English gardens and rolling hills. Each room has its own en-suite bathroom, decorated with Victorian tiles and claw-foot cast-iron tubs.
Outside, the gardens are lovingly landscaped, with gravel paths, stone fountains and a wide variety of plants and flowers typical of the English countryside. A wisteria-covered pergola provides a shady spot to relax, and a blue-tiled pool offers a refreshing escape from the occasional summer heat.
The mansion also features a games room with a pool table.

entries.name: #OFFICE
entries.content:
"Imperium Ride": It has a reception area with a sturdy wooden desk. On the desk, a typewriter gleams, ready to be used. Rotary telephones are lined up, and the sound of keys being pressed fills the air.
Neutral wallpapers line the walls, and paintings of landscapes or portraits of founders adorn the space. The floor is covered with linoleum tiles, sturdy and practical.
Private offices have large, solid wood desks, with leather swivel chairs, and desk lamps with brass bases. Wall calendars and inboxes for correspondence are essential elements. Employees are dressed formally: men in suits and ties, and women in dresses and low heels.
Meeting rooms have long conference tables surrounded by chairs, where presentations are made on large chalk boards. There are no projectors or digital equipment; visual presentations are made by hand.
In one corner, the break room has a steaming coffee pot and a small refrigerator for lunches. There are magazines and newspapers on a low table, and a few employees chat while taking a break, smoking cigarettes, since it was common to smoke indoors at that time.
The office files are organized in large metal cabinets, with folders carefully labeled. Documents are stored in paper form, and each piece of important information has its assigned physical place.

entries.name: #HOSPITAL
entries.content:
Hospital "White Dove": The building is an imposing red brick structure, with large windows that let in natural light. Upon entering, you are greeted by a spacious lobby, with black and white tiled floors, and a reception desk with dark wood counters. The walls are decorated with paintings and educational posters about health and hygiene.
The hospital hallways are painted in soft shades of green and cream, and metal chairs are lined along the walls for visitors. Waiting rooms are filled with old magazines and posters promoting vaccination campaigns against diseases such as polio.
Operating rooms are equipped with round surgical lamps and stainless steel tables. Nurses wear white scrubs with caps and doctors wear white coats, symbolizing professionalism and cleanliness.
Patient rooms are shared, with several beds lined up and separated by curtains. Each bed has a small bedside table and a chair for visitors. The windows are adorned with lace curtains, adding a homey touch to the clinical setting.
In the pediatric section, children rest on small, brightly painted metal beds. There are simple toys and storybooks to entertain the little ones. The maternity section has private rooms where new mothers can rest with their newborns, swaddled in soft blankets.
On the ground floor, there is a cafeteria where visitors and staff can take a break. Tables are covered with checkered tablecloths and the aroma of freshly brewed coffee fills the air. A handwritten menu offers simple meals such as sandwiches and soups.
{{char}}'s brother is the future director of the hospital.
